Articles

Getting started

Getting started with ASMap

Build a linkage map from a set of marker scores in a few lines, then find your way around the rest of the documentation.

Function guides

Constructing a linkage map

The two construction functions, for a data frame of marker scores and for an R/qtl cross object, and the MSTmap parameters they share.

Pulling and pushing markers

Setting problematic markers aside before construction and reintroducing them afterwards, instead of discarding them permanently.

Diagnosing genotypes and markers

Numerical and graphical profiling of individual genotypes, markers and intervals, and the identification of genetic clones.

Heat maps

Displaying pairwise recombination fractions and LOD scores of linkage together, with a separate legend for each.

Manipulating linkage maps

Breaking, merging, subsetting and combining linkage maps, and fast estimation of genetic distances.

Worked example

Worked example I: construction

A barley backcross marker set taken from 3,023 unassigned markers through pre-construction diagnosis to a constructed map of nine linkage groups.

Worked example II: refinement

Continuing the barley backcross example: pushing the held-back markers into the map, merging linkage groups to the expected seven, and post-construction development including fine mapping.

Background

How the MSTmap algorithm works

The minimum spanning tree formulation behind ASMap: how markers are clustered into linkage groups, how they are ordered within a group, and how missing scores are imputed as part of the same algorithm.

Notes on the MSTmap algorithm

How genetic distances are calculated, and what the mvest.bc and detectBadData arguments actually do.
